source_text: Οὐκοῦν τὸ μέγιστον καὶ κορυφαιότατον τῶν πρὸς τὴν ζωὴν μαθημάτων ἀπὸ τῆς ἀρχῆς εὐθὺς ἐγκαταθέσθαι τῇ ψυχῇ ψυχῇ δεῖ, γνῶναι τὸν θεὸν τὸν αἰώνιον καὶ δοτῆρα αἰωνίων καὶ πρῶτον καὶ ὑπέρτατον καὶ ἕνα καὶ ἀγαθὸν θεόν. ὅν ἔστι κτήσασθαι διὰ γνώσεως καὶ καταλήψεως· αὕτη γὰρ ἄτρεπτος καὶ ἀσάλευτος ἀρχὴ καὶ κρηπὶς ζωῆς, ἐπιστήμη θεοῦ τοῦ ὄντως ὄντος καὶ τὰ ὄντα. τουτέστι τὰ αἰώνια, δωρουμένου, ἐξ οὗ καὶ τὸ εἶναι τοῖς ἄλλοις ὑπάρχει καὶ τὸ μεῖναι λαβεῖν. ἡ μὲν γὰρ τούτου ἄγνοια θάνατός ἐστιν, ἡ δὲ ἐπίγνωσις αὐτοῦ καὶ οἰκείωσις καὶ ἡ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀγάπη καὶ ἐξομοίωσις μόνη ζωή.
thought_title: Knowing the eternal God is the foundation of life
orientation: Clement is explaining the first and greatest lesson Jesus taught the rich man: to know the one eternal God who gives eternal life.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the greatest and highest of the lessons for life must be deposited in the soul right from the beginning: to know the eternal God and giver of eternal things and first and highest and one and good God. Whom it is possible to acquire through knowledge and comprehension; for this is an unchangeable and unshakable beginning and foundation of life, knowledge of God who truly is and who gives the things that are, that is, the eternal things, from whom both being exists for other things and receiving remaining. For ignorance of him is death, but recognition of him and kinship and love toward him and likeness alone is life.

choices.why: The verb means to store or deposit something within; the dative ψυχῇ marks the soul as the receptacle, so 'deposited in the soul' preserves the spatial metaphor of placing a foundation within.
rejected: be laid up for the soul

choices.why: δοτήρ is a poetic noun for giver; αἰωνίων is a neuter plural substantive meaning eternal things, not eternal life specifically, so the literal rendering keeps the breadth.
κατάληψις is a Stoic technical term for firm grasping of a truth; 'comprehension' preserves the intellectual act of seizing hold of knowledge.
οἰκείωσις denotes being made a member of the household or family, a relational closeness; 'kinship' captures the familial bond with God that Clement contrasts with mere knowledge.
ἐξομοίωσις means becoming like or assimilation; 'likeness' is the standard rendering for the state of being made like God.
The participle ὄντα is a philosophical term for real beings; Clement glosses it as eternal things, so the literal rendering preserves the ontological weight.

pass_b_english: So the greatest and highest of the lessons that lead to life must be deposited in the soul right from the start: to know the eternal God, the giver of eternal things, the first and highest and one and good God. He is to be acquired through knowledge and comprehension. For this is the unchangeable and unshakable beginning and foundation of life: the understanding of God who truly is, and who gives the things that are—that is, the eternal things—from whom all other beings receive both their existence and their continuance. Ignorance of him is death, but the knowledge of him, and kinship with him, and love toward him, and likeness to him—this alone is life.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἡ μὲν γὰρ τοῦτοῦ ἄγνοια θάνατός ἐστιν
last_rejected.why: Greek says ignorance of “this” (the knowledge), not ignorance of God.
last_rejected.ruling: Τούτου refers to θεοῦ (v.2), not γνώσεως. 'Ignorance of him' = ignorance of God, matching the contrast with ἐπίγνωσις αὐτοῦ.
